current_episode.title: Building the Future: Leadership, Workforce Development & Growth in Construction (Marissa Bankert, President & CEO, Associated Builders and Contractors Eastern Pennsylvania (ABC Eastern PA))

guest.entreprise: Associated Builders and Contractors Eastern Pennsylvania
guest.bio_context: Marissa Bankert has built her career in association management, starting as a membership director in a realtors association before moving into the construction sector as an executive director working with independent electrical contractors. She has been in her current role as CEO of ABC Eastern PA for just over a year, bringing experience in mentorship, volunteer leadership at board level, and deep passion for positioning construction as the foundation of the nation.

context.real_quote: Construction really is the foundation of our nation. Whether you're a laborer or a CEO, you're all helping to weave that fabric that we all walk upon every single day.

context.transcript_excerpt: Welcome to the Think Small Podcast, hyper growth for small businesses. So, what's slowing you down? Well, hi again, everybody. This is Rob Godlevsky with the Think Small Podcast. And today we have a very special guest. This is Marissa Bankert. She is the CEO of the Associated Builders and Contractors of Eastern Pennsylvania. Marissa, thank you so much for joining us on the Think Small Podcast. My pleasure to be here. Thank you so much. Really looking forward to a great conversation. Oh, yeah, this will be fun. So you're a trade association that supports builders and contractors, specifically in eastern Pennsylvania, right? So Philadelphia and surrounding areas. That's right. But you're part of a broader national organization that supports builders and contractors throughout the country, right? That's exactly right. We're part of a 67-chapter network, covers the entirety of the United States and territories like Guam. And so it's really great to have that full network of people that I can turn to as a peer network, but also for our members to have that resource as well. As you know, construction is a pretty fluid business. So if they're not working inside of this geographic area, it's good to know that they could potentially bid on a project in Iowa and still have, you know, someone that they can turn to, find contractors who are a part of the ABC network to work with. Outstanding. So let's talk about Eastern Pennsylvania specifically, right? And the areas you're in charge. Tell us about what problems you solve for your members, you know, what your offerings are for your members, and then talk a little bit about how you got here, right? What is your journey into your leadership role here with the organization? Yeah, sure. So at ABC Eastern PA, we cover 17 counties. So kind of everything from the New York border to the Delaware border along the eastern part of the state here. And really, I think the key things that members come to us for are things like education and apprenticeship. We have several registered apprenticeship programs with the state of Pennsylvania. So our members are really interested in ensuring that future generations understand skilled trades and the workforce dynamic, you know, kind of surrounding that. So we get a lot of interest in that. The education also goes, as I affectionately say, from apprenticeship to ownership, right? So we're talking about those types of both technical education, leadership education, business acumen. So we're constantly kind of trying to provide all of those types of opportunities for our members to participate in. They obviously love some networking. It's so interesting. I think in a post-COVID world that some people don't necessarily think about networking as being the same way. We find it to be one of the highlights for our members. They are really engaged. They're attending events. They're participating in those kinds of things because they want that kind of opportunity to have those, you know, kind of at the table discussions with one another that can't transpire in the same way as, you know, you can in other methodologies. So we definitely love to bring our people together. That's a big value proposition for our members. And then we also offer things like, you know, discounts on the things that they're using most, like fuel and hotel rooms and FedEx and all of those kinds of things. Yeah. So it's just this, you know, kind of like menu of offerings, as it were, Rob, that we really present to the construction industry to try to help them navigate through whatever their issues are. You know, everything from understanding the legal side of construction, all the way over to, you know, the, hey, I just want to get together with my peers and have that conversation. And then for me, my journey has always been in association management. I'm thrilled to say that that's where I've built my career. And so for me, I started with as a membership director inside of a realtors association.

pending_qa.q: How can construction associations support members during periods of industry contraction and uncertainty?
pending_qa.r: During COVID, ABC Eastern PA served as the voice of members to legislators and government officials, helping them understand industry needs from an advocacy standpoint. The organization also acted as a resource driver, sourcing PPE like masks and hand sanitizer, and bringing together safety groups so contractors could share best practices on implementing new safety protocols.

pending_qa.q: What strategies help construction contractors navigate rapid growth and business expansion?
pending_qa.r: Marissa Bankert emphasizes the importance of coaching resources where business owners can develop plans to manage rapid growth, and peer groups where contractors can sit together and discuss shared challenges like labor shortages and estimator availability. She notes that having peer networks and mirrors held up to your business prevents unsustainable expansion.

pending_qa.q: What sectors are driving construction growth in Eastern Pennsylvania through 2026 and beyond?
pending_qa.r: Data centers are a major driver, with Pennsylvania recently publishing new guidelines welcoming this construction type. Life sciences and pharmaceutical construction in the Lehigh Valley represent significant opportunity. Healthcare, senior living, and multifamily residential continue to grow, while manufacturing and logistics may see modest decline but not monumental shifts.

pending_qa.q: How are construction labor market challenges being addressed through wage realignment in the industry?
pending_qa.r: Construction industry peers are resetting wage standards as a means to attract talent and fill hundreds of thousands of open jobs nationwide. Rather than viewing wages as fixed, contractors recognize that adjusting compensation upward becomes the new operating standard necessary to compete for workers and fulfill project backlogs.

pending_qa.q: What operational priorities is ABC Eastern PA pursuing to strengthen its position as the trusted voice for construction in Eastern Pennsylvania?
pending_qa.r: In her first year as CEO, Marissa Bankert focused on operational excellence, building processes and people capacity for the next phase. The organization aims to ramp up apprenticeship programs to solve workforce pipeline issues, expand pre-apprenticeship pathways to bring workers from other industries, and intensify focus on safety culture as a core member value.
